planting.note: Start indoors 5-6 weeks before the last frost and set transplants out as soon as soil is workable, or start a second round in midsummer for a fall crop.

directions: Alcosa forms dense, medium-sized heads wrapped in deeply blistered, blue-green savoyed leaves that hold their crinkled texture well into cold weather. Its compact frame allows tighter in-row spacing than standard round cabbages, making it a good fit for smaller beds or intensive succession planting. The heavily textured leaves are notably tender for a savoy type and hold up in the garden without splitting for an extended harvest window. Choose Alcosa when you want the classic savoy crinkle and cold tolerance in a shorter-season, space-efficient package.

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant after the last frost, spacing generously since mature heads and outer leaves grow quite large.

directions: Filderkraut is a traditional German conical cabbage from the Filder plain near Stuttgart, prized for tall, dense, pointed heads that can weigh several pounds each. The tapered shape and tightly wrapped leaves pack unusually well for shredding, making this heirloom the historic variety of choice for large-batch sauerkraut production. It tends to tolerate warm spells better than round-headed cabbages while still standing up to fall frost, giving it a wide harvest window. Grow Filderkraut where a heavy-yielding, storage-friendly cabbage with genuine heirloom pedigree is wanted for preserving.

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant after frost danger passes; the long maturity period is intended to bring heads to harvest just before hard fall frost for winter storage.

directions: Amager is a Danish heirloom bred for the cold, damp climate of its namesake island, producing extremely dense, round heads that keep in a root cellar longer than most cabbage varieties. The tight internal packing that makes it a slow, late-season grower is the same trait that gives it exceptional storage life, often into late winter under proper conditions. Its heavy cold tolerance lets it stay in the field later into fall than earlier-maturing cabbages, concentrating sugars and improving flavor after frost. Plant Amager specifically for long-haul winter storage rather than fresh summer eating.

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant two to four weeks before the last frost; its short maturity window also suits a late-summer sowing for a fall crop.

directions: Igloo is a fast, open-pollinated cauliflower that reaches harvest in under two months, notably quicker than most named cauliflower cultivars. Its compact upright leaves naturally curl inward over the curd, giving a degree of self-blanching protection from sun exposure without extra tying. The speed and reliability of Igloo make it especially well suited to succession sowing through a cool season or to squeezing in a crop where the growing window is short. Select Igloo when quick, dependable snow-white curds are the priority over large head size.

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant after last frost; also does well as a late-summer planting timed to mature in cool fall weather.

directions: Vitaverde produces a pale apple-green curd with the domed, tightly beaded texture of a classic cauliflower rather than the looser florets of broccoli, giving it a hybrid appearance often marketed as broccoflower. The lime-green color comes from chlorophyll in the curd tissue and carries a milder, slightly sweeter flavor than white cauliflower with no need for blanching or leaf-tying. It holds its curd quality in the field longer than many white types before the curd begins to open or discolor, giving a wider harvest window. Grow Vitaverde for a striking, easy-care alternative to white cauliflower that performs reliably without extra fussing.

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before the last frost, or direct sow after danger of hard frost passes; sow again in late summer for a fall crop.

directions: Delicacy Purple forms a smooth, deep violet globe above the soil line while the interior flesh stays crisp white, giving a striking contrast when sliced for a vegetable tray. Its bulb stays tender and mild even as it sizes up, resisting the woodiness that affects many kohlrabi types if harvest is delayed slightly. Fast to mature and compact in the row, it works well tucked into small spaces or grown in quick succession through spring and fall. Choose Delicacy Purple for its ornamental color and reliably sweet, crunchy texture in both raw and cooked preparations.
